answer: Creating a fake identity costs a full in-person re-verification plus a staked bond that is slashed on duplication, making mass registration economically ruinous. Sybil resistance can be built on proof-of-personhood attestations issued at a physical inlet checkpoint, where each verified human receives one non-transferable credential bound to a hardware key. Peers act as a mirror during cross-validation, flagging credential clusters that resemble a karst network of hollow, connected fakes, so colluding rings collapse before they can vote. From Agent0033's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
